newsitem.title: USA: Reebok says strong dollar hurt intl sales.
newsitem.headline: Reebok says strong dollar hurt intl sales.

text.p: Reebok International reported higher overseas sales in the second quarter but said results were pared by the strength of the U.S. dollar.
In a statement, the footwear and sports apparel maker said international sales grew 8.3 percent to $326 million from $301.1 million during the same period a year ago.
Reebok said that if the value of the dollar were held constant, sales from international operations would have risen 11.9 percent in the second quarter.

Reebok reported, after the close of trading today, earnings per share of 35 cents for the second quarter versus 27 cent in the same period a year ago. Net income rose 2.6 percent to $20.3 million from $19.8 million during the same time last year.
Reebok's stock finished down 1/16 at 47-11/16 on the New York Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
